chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Wallad, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was killed and who had children, some minors and some adults. What do you say if his adult children pardon?

He said: “He is not to be killed, and the pardon of the adult children is valid regarding their own shares. Then when the minors grow up, they have the right to demand their shares of the blood money.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money paid as legal compensation for killing
key_terms.الصِّغَارُ: the minor children who have not yet reached maturity
key_terms.الْكِبَارُ: the adult children among the heirs
key_terms.حِصَصِهِمْ: their respective legal shares in the claim
key_terms.عَفَا: pardoned or waived the right of retaliation
key_terms.لَا يُقْتَلُ: the killer is not subjected to execution in this case

ai.seo_question: If some heirs of a murder victim are adults and others are minors, can the adults pardon the killer on behalf of everyone?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the heirs of a murder victim when some are adults and others are minors. The adult heirs may waive their own shares of retribution, but this does not cancel the rights of the minors; when they reach maturity, they may claim their shares from the diyah.
